gen-gf-wallpoet-fs-fira-sans: Fira Sans has a generous x-height and curves that swing wide open, drawn with hardly any thick-to-thin shift. Wallpoet sits above it, bold and commanding, and a long page of the body text would glide along without snagging.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-satoshi: Gappy, striking letters that break every word apart. Electroharmonix earns its place in big, short lines, while Satoshi's soaring x-height and open e keep the text beneath it approachable, its strokes cut to one width.
gen-dafont-joystix-fs-supreme: Supreme sets a crisp, dense-looking band of text, its curves held open instead of curling shut. Joystix adds a wide-tracked arcade shout above it, and the two sit together with a clear job each.
gen-dafont-nasalization-general-sans: Nasalization floats its letters well apart, with short ascenders and a c opened like calipers. General Sans follows with a smooth pen pressure and a tall x-height, which makes the pairing feel friendly yet businesslike.
gen-dafont-nordic-work-sans: Nordic spaces its letters like brush dabs far apart, with a cramped, closed look and a single stroke weight. Work Sans opens everything back up, its c tips staying apart, and that closed-versus-open tension is the pair's best trick.
gen-dafont-stencilia-switzer: Switzer brings tubular, wire-like letters and a tall waist line, with c tips that stay well apart. And Stencilia, structural and striking, adds spacious gaps at its curve ends, so the two sit together as a crisp, deliberate duo.
gen-dafont-groovy-manrope: Manrope reads bright and approachable, with a gap at every curve's mouth. And Groovy, friendly and funky with its near-shut c, gives a long page of the sans-serif text a playful lead-in without ever crowding it.
gen-gf-warnes-archivo: Archivo brings an editorial, approachable feel, its curves opening outward under a commanding x-height. Archivo's openness against Warnes, with its tapering ink strokes and stretched tracking, is the quality that makes this pair work.
gen-gf-warnes-fs-asap: Stretched, bold, and drawn in one stroke width. Asap answers with open arcs and a body height nearly matching its capitals, so Warnes gets to be the loud one while the text stays readable.
gen-gf-warnes-fs-epilogue: Warnes stretches out, bold and tapered, with ink strokes that never quite touch. Epilogue follows with curvy, unclamped letters and a wire-like skeleton, so a long page of it would flow along easily.
